about: Cited corrections applied by tools/build_isaref.py on top of the raw Ruby dump (emips/data/instructions.json, never hand-edited). Real MIPS wins: every entry cites the MIPS32 manual and was cross-checked with tools/audit_isa_binutils.py.

references.II-A: MIPS32 Architecture For Programmers, Volume II-A: The MIPS32 Instruction Set Manual (MD00086), Revision 5.04 -- instruction pages and Appendix A 'Instruction Bit Encodings'
references.IV-e: MIPS Architecture for Programmers Volume IV-e: The MIPS DSP Module for the MIPS32 Architecture (MD00374), Revision 3.01 -- chapter 5 'Instruction Encoding' and the chapter 6 instruction pages
references.dsp cross-check: GNU binutils opcodes/mips-opc.c (ASE_DSP = D32, ASE_DSPR2 = D33, ASE_DSPR3 = D34) and tools/audit_isa_binutils.py
references.IV-f: MIPS Architecture for Programmers Volume IV-f: The MIPS MT Module for the MIPS32 Architecture (MD00378), Revision 1.12 -- chapter 5 instruction pages (DMT, DVPE, EMT, EVPE, FORK, MFTR, MTTR, YIELD)
references.mt cross-check: GNU binutils opcodes/mips-opc.c (ASE_MT = MT32) and tools/audit_isa_binutils.py

corrections.name: LWL
corrections.ref: II-A LWL; II-A App. A, 'MIPS32 Encoding of the Opcode Field'
corrections.why: Ruby table carried LH's opcode 100001; LWL is opcode 100010. With the old key LWL tied with LH and could never decode.

corrections.name: SWC2
corrections.ref: II-A SWC2; II-A App. A, 'MIPS32 Encoding of the Opcode Field'
corrections.why: Ruby table carried SWC1's opcode 111001; SWC2 is opcode 111010. With the old key SWC2 tied with SWC1 and could never decode.
